title: Leveraging Soft Prompts for Privacy Attacks in Federated Prompt Tuning
abstract: arXiv:2601.06641v4 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Membership inference attacks (MIAs) pose a serious privacy threat in federated learning (FL). While MIAs have been extensively studied in standard FL, the recent shift toward federated fine-tuning introduces new and largely unexplored attack surfaces. In this work, we show that federated prompt-tuning, which adapts pre-trained foundation models using lightweight input prefixes, exposes a novel and effective vector for membership inference. We propose PromptMIA, a membership inference attack tailored to federated prompt-tuning, in which a malicious server introduces adversarially crafted prompts and exploits their updates during collaborative training to determine whether a target data point belongs to a client's private dataset. We formalize this threat via a security game and demonstrate that PromptMIA achieves consistently high attack advantage across diverse benchmark datasets, substantially outperforming current SOTA federated MI

translated_title: 利用软提示在联邦提示调优中实施隐私攻击
translated_abstract: 成员推理攻击（MIAs）在联邦学习（FL）中构成了严重的隐私威胁。尽管MIAs在标准联邦学习场景下已被广泛研究，但近期向联邦微调的转变引入了新的、在很大程度上尚未被探索的攻击面。在本工作中，我们证明了联邦提示调优——一种通过轻量级输入前缀来适配预训练基础模型的方法——暴露了一种新颖且高效的成员推理攻击途径。我们提出了PromptMIA，一种专为联邦提示调优量身定制的成员推理攻击：恶意服务器注入对抗性构造的提示，并在协作训练过程中利用这些提示的更新来判断某个目标数据点是否属于客户端的私有数据集。我们通过安全博弈对这一威胁进行了形式化定义，并证明PromptMIA在多种基准数据集上均能持续取得较高的攻击优势，显著优于当前最先进的联邦成员推理攻击方法。
tldr: 提出了PromptMIA——一种针对联邦提示调优的新型成员推理攻击，恶意服务器通过注入对抗性构造的软提示并利用其训练更新，能够高效地推断出客户端私有数据集中的成员信息，显著优于现有联邦学习攻击方法。
en_tdlr: PromptMIA, a novel membership inference attack tailored to federated prompt-tuning, in which a malicious server injects adversarially crafted soft prompts and exploits their training updates to accurately determine whether target data points belong to clients' private datasets, substantially outperforming existing state-of-the-art federated MIA methods.
